name: Dify
tagline: Open source platform for building AI apps with RAG
description: Open source platform for building production-ready AI applications, with a visual flow builder, a knowledge base that cites sources and execution tracing.
priceNote: Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Teams that need to put an assistant grounded in their documents live
pros: Ready knowledge base: import PDFs, sites and manuals, and the agent answers citing the source
Open source, with self-hosting possible, which gives control over data and predictable cost
Visual builder with prompt, condition, code and HTTP nodes, so logic does not require a developer
Publishes the app as an API or as a ready chat widget to embed on your site
cons: Self-hosting requires a server, containers and someone who updates the image and watches security
The visual builder struggles with complex logic, and then the team ends up writing code in the code node
Message credits cover part of the model usage, and anything above the quota runs on your API key, billed per token
Documentation and community are still mostly in English, which is hard for local teams

features.name: Knowledge base
features.detail: Indexes PDFs, sites and text and answers with the highlighted source passage

features.name: Visual flow
features.detail: Prompt, condition, list, code and HTTP request nodes chained together

features.name: Multi-model
features.detail: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, local models and Ollama in the same interface

features.name: Publishing and widget
features.detail: Delivers the app as a REST API or as an embedded chat on your site

features.name: Plugin marketplace
features.detail: Ready extensions for tools, models and data providers

useCases: Internal assistant that answers questions about product manuals, policy and employment contracts
Website chatbot that answers from the documentation base and escalates to a human when needed
Sales tool that queries the catalog and the price sheet and builds the proposal
Document classifier that extracts invoice and contract fields before they enter the ERP
bestForWho: Companies that want an AI assistant grounded in their own documents, with the option to run everything inside their own infrastructure.
verdict: Dify is the best-positioned middle ground between open code and a finished product, and the knowledge base with citations is what makes it beat conversational-only platforms. When the flow is simple, it ships a live, working application in days with no engineering team. The wall arrives when the logic gets complex: the visual builder accepts it, but then you are using the code node and back to normal development. For a small company, the Community edition on a VPS works and the license is free, but all model consumption is on your account. For a larger company, the cloud Professional plan delivers SSO, environments and team management, and it is still worth confirming where the infrastructure sits before you put client data inside it.
